premises: Nanoscale clusters of Cr, Ni, and Mn form at grain boundaries in CrMnFeCoNi during intermediate-temperature aging.
These nanoclusters reduce grain-boundary cohesive strength.
Reduced cohesion promotes intergranular crack initiation and a ductile-to-brittle transition.
This embrittlement mechanism is distinct from conventional grain-boundary precipitation.
